Class NativeWinWindowControl

java.lang.Object
com.meshtastic.client.platform.NativeWinWindowControl
public class NativeWinWindowControl extends Object
Windows Mica/Acrylic control through the DWM API.

Windows 11 22H2+: DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE from dwmapi.dll provides the system Acrylic/Mica backdrop. Windows 10 falls back to SetWindowCompositionAttribute from user32.dll with ACCENT_ENABLE_ACRYLICBLURBEHIND.

Together with StageStyle.TRANSPARENT this gives the app a custom title bar, matching the macOS implementation, and a blurred backdrop.

Dragging and resizing are handled by RootPane through JavaFX EventFilters.

  • Method Details

    • initDarkModeSupport

      public static void initDarkModeSupport()
      Initializes Windows 10 dark-mode support. Call this once before creating the window.

      On Windows 10, DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE is ignored unless the undocumented uxtheme.dll ordinal 135 (SetPreferredAppMode) is called first. On Windows 11 these calls are harmless.

    • extendFrameIntoClientArea

      public boolean extendFrameIntoClientArea()
      Extends the DWM frame over the entire client area. MARGINS{-1,-1,-1,-1} creates a "sheet of glass": the DWM surface covers the full client area and lets the backdrop show through it.

    • setWindowBackdrop

      public boolean setWindowBackdrop(NativeWinWindowControl.DwmSystemBackdropType backdrop)
      Applies a system backdrop: Mica, Mica Alt, Acrylic, or None. Windows 11 22H2+.

    • setDarkMode

      public boolean setDarkMode(boolean dark)
      Enables or disables dark mode for the title bar.

      Strategy, from preferred path to fallbacks: 1. DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE (attribute 20) on Win10 20H1+ and Win11 2. DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE (attribute 19) on Win10 1809-18985 3. DWMWA_CAPTION_COLOR (attribute 35) on Win11 22000+, with an explicit caption color

      Raw Pointer + Memory is used instead of BOOLByReference to guarantee that DwmSetWindowAttribute receives the expected LPCVOID payload.

    • setCaptionColor

      public boolean setCaptionColor(int colorRef)
      Sets the caption bar color directly. COLORREF format: 0x00BBGGRR. Available on Win11 22000+ and non-fatal on Win10.

    • applyPlainDecoratedTitleBar

      public void applyPlainDecoratedTitleBar(boolean isDark)
      Native DECORATED title bar without backdrop effects. On Win11 the standard dark title bar visually resembles Mica, so when effects are disabled we set an explicit solid caption color.

    • redrawFrame

      public void redrawFrame()
      Forces the non-client area, including the title bar, to repaint.

      A WM_NCACTIVATE deactivate/activate cycle makes Windows repaint the title bar with the latest DWM attributes, including dark mode. SWP_FRAMECHANGED alone is not enough on Win10: it recalculates the frame but does not repaint the caption.

    • setRoundedCorners

      public boolean setRoundedCorners()
      Enables rounded corners on Windows 11+. Non-fatal on Win10.

    • setAcrylicViaCompositionAttribute

      public boolean setAcrylicViaCompositionAttribute(boolean isDark)
      Applies Acrylic blur through SetWindowCompositionAttribute (user32.dll). This undocumented API works with layered windows created by StageStyle.TRANSPARENT.

      ACCENT_POLICY: {AccentState, AccentFlags, GradientColor(ABGR), AnimationId}, 16 bytes. WINDOWCOMPOSITIONATTRIBDATA: {Attribute(int), pad, pData(ptr), cbData(size_t)}.

      Parameters:
      isDark - dark theme uses a dark tint; light theme uses a light tint
      Returns:
      true if Acrylic blur was applied successfully

    • prepareMicaWindow

      public boolean prepareMicaWindow(boolean isDark)
      Prepares the window for a blurred backdrop.

      Strategy: Windows 11 22H2+ uses DWMWA_SYSTEMBACKDROP_TYPE for system Acrylic; Windows 10 falls back to SetWindowCompositionAttribute with ACCENT_ENABLE_ACRYLICBLURBEHIND.

      This does not modify window styles such as WS_CAPTION. StageStyle.TRANSPARENT provides the borderless window, while JavaFX RootPane handles drag and resize.

      Returns:
      true if the backdrop was applied successfully
